html:
The Bundjalung are an Aboriginal Australian nation of the far north coast of New South Wales and the edge of southeast Queensland. Their country runs from the Clarence River north to the Tweed and inland to the ranges, and takes in the Richmond River and today's Byron Bay.

The Bundjalung language had many dialects, spoken by a cluster of related clans. Their neighbours were the Yugambeh to the north, the Ngarabal on the tablelands and the Gumbaynggirr to the south. The volcanic peak Wollumbin, called Mount Warning in English, is a sacred place.

From the 1840s cedar cutters worked up the rivers felling red cedar, and sheep and cattle runs followed. Sugar cane and dairy farms later filled the river valleys.
